items.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024
items.q: I have my music, I get to choose who’s there, including my sister.

ctx.x: The one female musician and isn’t that wonderful?

Yes. I’ve worked over there too. I was the one female musician too. So, and I’m guilty of it myself. I’m surrounding myself with mostly men in a big band but at least I have my music, I have control over some of the situation. I have my music, I get to choose who’s there, including my sister. I get to play in it this way. I get to play whatever I want. And I’ve kind of created my own circumstances for this to happen and I can’t say that it’s a bad thing because the other thing was like going, “Oh I just really…

other stuff aside and went if you want me it’s about what I have to offer as a composer and a musician I guess. I mean sometimes I get — don’t get me wrong, I love to be able to sit down and play through a set of great — someone else’s music that’s really fun like give me Jim McNeely’s book any day or the Vanguard book. I would just love to be a part of that. But my path just kind of wove in a different direction because — probably because of just privilege and opportunity and those two lacking things at times…
